Interface Design Research

Comparative Exploration of Augmented Reality SDKs for Interactive Content Development

Vuforia, ARFoundation, Lightship ARDK & MindAR.js — A Practical Laboratory Study
Authors: Elkin Andres Aldana Villafañe · Sebastian Ñustes · Santiago Amezquita Program: Software Engineering · Universidad Manuela Beltrán Guide: #9 — RA SDKs · 2026 Sessions: 2 (Unity + Web AR)
Abstract

This article documents the practical implementation of five AR software development kits within the Interface Design course at Universidad Manuela Beltrán. Over two laboratory sessions, eight distinct AR exercises were developed: image recognition, ground plane detection, cylinder tracking, surface interaction, hand tracking, semantic segmentation, web-based image tracking, and facial accessory overlays.

Results demonstrate complementary strengths across SDKs: Vuforia provides robust Unity-integrated marker tracking; ARFoundation enables cross-platform gesture interaction; Lightship ARDK unlocks advanced perception; and MindAR.js democratizes AR deployment via the browser with no installation required.

Keywords: Augmented Reality · Vuforia · ARFoundation · Lightship ARDK · MindAR.js · Unity · Web AR · Image Tracking · Hand Tracking

1. Introduction

Augmented Reality combines real-world visualization with virtual elements generated by an electronic device, creating a mixed reality. As AR technologies mature, software engineering programs face both the opportunity and responsibility to incorporate these tools into curricula.

This report covers Laboratory Guide #9, in which students implemented exercises across Vuforia, ARFoundation, Lightship ARDK, and MindAR.js with A-Frame.

2. Problem Statement

Studies on scientific experimentation in the classroom when designing and producing AR objects remain scarce. Experimental knowledge is essential for students to achieve deeper understanding and ownership of knowledge.

Central question: How can the Software Engineering program's teaching-learning process be strengthened through AR technologies that enable autonomous knowledge construction?

3. Objectives

General

Design, develop, and evaluate AR objects to support teaching and learning within the Interface Design course.

Specific

1

Define functional requirements for AR object creation based on topics from the degree program.

2

Design interaction elements based on requirements and user-centered design principles.

3

Develop AR objects using evaluated tools across Unity and web platforms.

4

Evaluate AR objects using heuristic and empirical assessment methods.

4. AR Types Implemented

Marker-Based

Printed image targets (flat or cylindrical) as anchors for 3D content — via Vuforia Image Target, Cylinder Target, and MindAR.js image tracking.

Surface / Ground Plane

Detects horizontal surfaces to anchor 3D models without markers — Vuforia Ground Plane Stage and ARFoundation Plane + Raycast Manager.

Body / Face Tracking

Detects anatomical landmarks — hand skeleton joints via Lightship ARDK, and 468 facial mesh points via MindAR Face.

Web-Based

Browser-native AR using MindAR.js + A-Frame over HTTPS, with no native installation required.

5. Exercises Implemented

Session 1 — Unity

Vuforia SDK — Exercise 1: Image Target

Image Target configured in Unity to detect the lab cover and superimpose two animated BlueFigure characters using the Vuforia Engine and Unity prefab system.

Fig. 1 — Vuforia Image Target: two animated characters superimposed on the detected lab cover in Unity Editor.
Vuforia SDK — Exercise 2: Ground Plane

Ground Plane Stage detects horizontal surfaces to anchor an animated robot using the Plane Finder and Animator Controller.

Fig. 2 — Vuforia Ground Plane: animated robot anchored on a detected horizontal surface.
ARFoundation — Touch Interaction

AR Plane Manager + AR Raycast Manager combined with custom C# scripts to enable multi-touch select, move, rotate, and scale interactions.

Fig. 3 — ARFoundation: red cube with gesture-based selection, movement, rotation, and scaling on a detected AR plane.
Lightship ARDK — Hand Tracking & Segmentation

Extends ARFoundation with hand skeleton tracking (HumanHandTracker) and semantic segmentation classifying environment regions for selective visual effects.

Fig. 4 — Lightship ARDK: hand skeleton landmarks detected — Detection Status: Confirmed.

Session 2 — Web AR (MindAR.js)

MindAR.js — Web AR Portfolio

Built with MindAR.js v1.2.5 + A-Frame v1.3.0. A custom image target triggers a rotating cube, orbiting sphere, animated text, and skill indicators.

Fig. 5 — MindAR.js + A-Frame: web AR portfolio with purple cube and green sphere over an image target.
MindAR.js — Face Tracking + Accessories

MindAR Face detects 468 facial mesh landmarks. Accessories — glasses (anchor 168), crown (anchor 10), earrings (anchors 234 & 454) — toggled via a UI panel.

Fig. 6 — MindAR Face Tracking: accessories at facial anchor points with interactive toggle panel.

7. Conclusions

C1

Vuforia offers robust Unity integration for image, ground-plane, and cylinder tracking with a moderate learning curve.

C2

ARFoundation enables cross-platform AR from a single Unity project, reducing development time for multi-device targets.

C3

MindAR.js democratizes AR access by running natively in the browser with no installation — ideal for educational deployments.

C4

Face tracking with 468 facial mesh landmarks enables simultaneous, high-precision accessory placement at multiple anchor points.

C5

Web AR requires HTTPS for camera access — platforms like Netlify provide convenient rapid deployment for student projects.
